title: Circuit Breaker Pattern: Stop Cascading Failures
intro: In distributed systems, a single failing service can take down others. Learn how the Circuit Breaker pattern prevents cascading failures and keeps your system resilient.

slides.heading: The Problem
slides.subtitle: Cascading failures in microservices.
slides.explain: Imagine one microservice calls another. If the called service is slow or unresponsive, the calling service waits. If many calls to the failing service pile up, the calling service's resources get exhausted, eventually causing it to fail too. This can spread quickly.
points: Service B fails or is slow.
Service A exhausts resources and fails.

slides.heading: What It Is
slides.subtitle: A safety mechanism for service calls.
slides.explain: The Circuit Breaker pattern is like an electrical circuit breaker. When a service experiences too many failures (e.g., timeouts, errors) within a set period, the circuit "trips" open. Instead of retrying the failing service, requests immediately fail fast or fall back to a default.

slides.heading: Circuit States
slides.subtitle: Closed, Open, and Half-Open.
slides.explain: It operates in three states. Closed is normal. Too many failures shift it to Open, where all requests fail fast. After a timeout, it tries Half-Open with a few test requests. If successful, back to Closed; if not, back to Open.
points: Open: Block all calls for a duration.

slides.heading: How It Helps
slides.subtitle: Improves resilience and responsiveness.
slides.explain: By failing fast when a downstream service is struggling, the calling service saves its own resources. It avoids tying up threads, memory, and CPU waiting for an unresponsive service. This allows the calling service to remain operational and serve other requests or use fallback mechanisms.
points: Allows time for failing service to recover.

slides.heading: Fallbacks & Metrics
slides.subtitle: Graceful degradation and insights.
slides.explain: When the circuit is open, you can provide a fallback response, like cached data, a default value, or an empty list. This ensures a degraded but still functional experience. Circuit breakers also provide metrics on success/failure rates, giving insights into service health.

scenario.situation: Your e-commerce microservice calls a third-party payment gateway to finalize orders.
scenario.problem: The payment gateway fails. Your service's payment calls hang, exhausting connection pools and crashing your entire order processing service.
scenario.fix: A Circuit Breaker detects payment gateway failures, trips open, and returns an error. Your order service continues processing, protected from the external outage. It avoids crashing.
scenario.takeaway: Circuit breakers prevent external failures from crashing your own system.
